articles.title: Home Assistant turns readings and actions into custom climate controls
articles.dek: A new helper combines chosen sensor readings and scripted actions into a heating or cooling control.
body: Home Assistant adds a way to build a custom heating or cooling control around existing readings and actions. The template integration supplies its displayed state from templates and runs configured scripts when someone changes a mode or target temperature.

Petro31 adds setup through the Helpers screen or YAML configuration. Options cover temperature, humidity, fan modes, presets and air-direction controls. The person configuring the helper supplies the readings and actions behind the features they need; automatic temperature regulation depends on those configured actions.

pullRequests.title: Add climate platform to template integration
Add climate platform to template integration

articles.title: Home Assistant keeps more private details out of troubleshooting logs
articles.dek: Four integrations stop recording router credentials, banking identifiers and tracked coordinates in specific log messages.
body: Home Assistant removes sensitive values from several messages that can end up in troubleshooting logs. Xiaomi router login failures stop recording the supplied username and password, and a failed Start.ca setup stops repeating the configured API key.

The National Weather Service integration also stops recording the coordinates of a followed person or device when it updates the weather station for that location. FinTS banking messages drop account numbers and the online-banking username while retaining the configured bank name.

Franck Nijhof’s corrections remove these particular exposures; they do not make every log free of private information. FinTS can still include an account number when it forms part of an entity’s existing name.

pullRequests.title: Do not log the Xiaomi router password
Do not log the Start.ca API key
Do not log IBANs and account numbers in FinTS
Do not log the tracked location in NWS

articles.title: Home Assistant lets you choose which calendars and lists Siri uses
articles.dek: Separate choices for each server control what Siri can access, and calendar queries refresh after changes.
body: Home Assistant’s Apple app gains separate choices for the calendars and to-do lists exposed to Siri. Each connected server has a configuration screen where people can switch individual lists on or off and choose their defaults.

Siri’s calendar queries also refresh the server’s events before answering, avoiding a stale response immediately after creating or changing an event. Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves adds the settings and refresh behavior; Spotlight continues to use its cached calendar information.

pullRequests.title: Choose which calendars and to-do lists Siri can use per server
Refresh cached calendar events before Siri reads them

articles.title: Music Assistant stops library checks from freezing sign-in
articles.dek: A recurring duplicate-track scan can block the whole library when thousands of tracks share a title.
body: Music Assistant fixes an hourly library check that could leave the interface stuck on “Authenticating.” Comparing thousands of tracks with the same title held up the database, stopping other library requests—including the count needed to finish signing in.

OzGav narrows duplicate checks to useful comparisons across different music sources and skips empty titles or titles shared by more than 200 tracks. In a test library of 40,000 tracks, with 6,000 sharing one title, the query fell from 55 seconds to under a second. A library with only one source skips the check entirely.
The original reporter confirmed that disabling the hourly check stopped the freezes. Marvin Schenkel reviewed the correction.

pullRequests.title: Keep the duplicate track walk from freezing the library database

articles.title: ESPHome gives Sendspin an off switch that survives a reboot
articles.dek: Disabling the client closes its connection and removes it from discovery until it is turned back on.
body: ESPHome devices gain a configurable switch for turning their Sendspin audio client off and back on. Switching it off closes the server connection and removes the device from Sendspin discovery on the network.

Kevin Ahrendt makes the switch remember its setting across a reboot. A disabled device waits for that saved setting before starting the client, avoiding a brief connection during startup. The switch defaults to on; while it is off, the device refuses playback and source commands.

pullRequests.title: [sendspin] Add a switch platform to enable and disable the client

articles.title: Apple Watch replies reach Home Assistant automations
articles.dek: A correction delivers typed notification answers that watchOS had silently dropped.
body: Typing an answer to a Home Assistant notification on Apple Watch could show a reply screen yet never send the answer home. The companion app handles those text-entry actions itself and delivers the entered text through the paired iPhone or the watch’s own connection.

Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves restores the notification events expected by automations. Actions requiring authentication remain under watchOS control, preserving that protection; older server-configured notification categories are unchanged.

pullRequests.title: Fix text input notification actions on Apple Watch

articles.title: Home Assistant restricts local access to its backup password
articles.dek: The saved backup configuration gains private file permissions, including a rewrite of existing stores.
body: Home Assistant tightens the permissions on the file holding its automatic-backup encryption password. Container and Core installations no longer leave that file readable by every local user; existing saved configurations are rewritten with private permissions when loaded.

The change preserves administrator access to the backup emergency kit. On Home Assistant OS it adds a precaution rather than a new boundary, because processes able to read the configuration directory already run with elevated access.
dbl-0 makes a first contribution to Home Assistant Core with the change.

pullRequests.title: Write the backup store with private=True so the backup password is not world-readable

articles.title: Music Assistant answers playback commands from Mac scripts
articles.dek: AppleScript can play, pause, skip and check the desktop app’s playback state.
body: Mac automation scripts gain a way to control Music Assistant’s desktop app. Its AppleScript interface accepts play, pause, stop, next-track and previous-track commands, and reports whether the player is playing, paused or stopped.
The commands use the app’s existing playback controls and follow Spotify’s scripting terminology. This is Paulus Schoutsen’s first contribution to the Music Assistant desktop-app repository.

articles.title: Music Assistant finds alternate albums on YouTube Music
articles.dek: The Other Versions view can retrieve editions that YouTube Music leaves out of search.
body: Music Assistant’s Other Versions view finds alternate editions of YouTube Music albums by asking the service for them directly. YouTube Music does not include those alternatives in its search results, making the view largely ineffective when it was the listener’s only music source.
Chris Roberts adds the lookup in his first contribution to the Music Assistant server, reviewed by Marvin Schenkel.

pullRequests.title: Properly surface "Other versions" of an album from Youtube Music

roadmapUpdates.title: Device database contributions reach approval review
roadmapUpdates.summary: The first web contribution workflow moves from Shaping to Awaiting approval. Matthias Kerstner adds a shared proposal; its scope includes storage, initial moderation and individual changes submitted through the website or public Git repository, excluding anonymous contributions.

sources.title: Enable first iteration of contributing to the device database via the web interface

roadmapUpdates.title: The Modbus connection panel enters Building
roadmapUpdates.summary: The plan for a Modbus panel moves from Approved to Building. It aims to show which connections and devices are reachable, with links to serial ports; adding or editing connections remains outside this first scope.

sources.title: Show a Modbus panel in the new Connectivity settings to provide an easy entry point

roadmapUpdates.title: Battery-free Zigbee switch support enters Building
roadmapUpdates.summary: The Green Power opportunity moves from Awaiting approval to Building after Matthias Kerstner asks whether its existing progress warrants the move. The plan covers pairing and managing battery-free, energy-harvesting devices in ZHA.

roadmapUpdates.title: Remote-control plans clarify their next steps
roadmapUpdates.summary: For receiving radio commands, Abílio Costa offers to investigate the missing design, then asks whether to wait for approval. Separately, Matthias Kerstner supports advancing the broader remote-device proposal led by DAB-LABS, although that card remains in Shaping.

sources.title: Turn any remote into a first-class Home Assistant device

roadmapUpdates.title: Finding the right infrared and radio adapter
roadmapUpdates.summary: Abílio Costa proposes separate documentation categories for integrations that provide infrared or radio transmitters and those that use them, plus a shared prerequisites note. The proxy-documentation opportunity remains in Building.

sources.title: Add documentation for proxying connectivity options

roadmapUpdates.title: Phone navigation proposal sets out a staged approach
roadmapUpdates.summary: Niels condenses Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves’s navigation proposal with his consent, outlining work on the shared frontend connection and iOS in one cycle, then Android in a follow-up. The approach remains under consideration and keeps existing dashboards intact.

sources.title: Give the companion app platform-standard navigation

roadmapUpdates.title: Apple still rejects the companion app transfer
roadmapUpdates.summary: Responding to the revised transfer guidance, Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves confirms he has already raised those points with Apple Developer Support, which still says the app is ineligible. The planned transfer to the foundation remains blocked.
